name: Compare Project Judgment Stats
description: Add project-level comparison stats, Human vs LLM conflict filters, Human vs LLM true-conflict filters, and summary-mode Cohen's kappa to the Compare Project Judgments page.

userStories.title: Add comparison stats calculation helpers
userStories.description: As a developer, I want reusable comparison stats helpers so conflict counts, true-conflict counts, and summary-mode kappa are calculated consistently from serving cells.
acceptanceCriteria: Create focused comparison stats helpers under the existing comparison project route helper area.
Stats helpers build comparison groups for primary-vs-human, every human-vs-LLM pair, and every LLM-vs-LLM pair.
Stats helpers compute overlapCount and conflictCount from non-empty normalized answers.
Stats helpers compute trueConflictCount by normalizing yes and maybe to include and no to exclude.
Stats helpers compute summary-mode Cohen's kappa only for exactly two summary raters using binary include/exclude decisions.
Stats helpers return cohensKappa as null for non-summary mode and multi-rater comparisons.
Unit tests cover no active generation, LLM-vs-LLM conflicts, human-vs-LLM conflicts, maybe-as-include true-conflict semantics, and summary-mode kappa.

userStories.title: Extend comparison difference filter contract
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the shared difference filter contract to include Human vs LLM true conflict and the renamed Human vs LLM conflict label so client and server use one filter vocabulary.
acceptanceCriteria: ComparisonProjectDifferenceFilter includes all, human-vs-llm, human-vs-llm-true-conflict, llm-vs-llm, and any-disagreement.
getComparisonProjectDifferenceFilterLabel returns Human vs LLM conflict for human-vs-llm.
getComparisonProjectDifferenceFilterLabel returns Human vs LLM true conflict for human-vs-llm-true-conflict.
getAvailableComparisonProjectDifferenceFilters includes human-vs-llm-true-conflict only when at least one human column and one LLM column are available.
Compare Project Judgments URL state preserves and normalizes differenceFilter=human-vs-llm-true-conflict.
Existing filter behavior for llm-vs-llm and any-disagreement is preserved.

userStories.title: Materialize Human vs LLM true conflicts
userStories.description: As a reviewer, I want Human vs LLM true conflicts materialized in comparison serving rows so true-conflict filtering and stats use the same data.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a DuckDB migration that updates or rebuilds mart.comparison_article_serving with has_human_vs_llm_true_conflict and passes_difference_filter_human_vs_llm_true_conflict.
The migration adds human-vs-llm-true-conflict support to mart.comparison_filter_member and mart.comparison_filter_stats.
The migration marks comparison serving stale so rows are rematerialized with the new fields.
The serving rollup builder normalizes yes and maybe to include and no to exclude for Human vs LLM true-conflict calculation.
The serving rollup builder sets has_human_vs_llm_true_conflict when any comparable Human vs LLM answer pair is include vs exclude.
Serving rollup tests cover yes vs no, maybe vs no, yes vs maybe, maybe vs maybe, and no vs no true-conflict behavior.

userStories.title: Wire Human vs LLM true-conflict filtering
userStories.description: As a reviewer, I want to filter Compare Project Judgments to Human vs LLM true conflicts so I can review only workflow-relevant conflicts.
acceptanceCriteria: The comparison judgments page endpoint accepts differenceFilter=human-vs-llm-true-conflict.
The comparison judgments count endpoint returns counts for human-vs-llm-true-conflict from mart.comparison_filter_stats.
The comparison export endpoint applies human-vs-llm-true-conflict with the same semantics as the table endpoint.
Filtered rows include Human vs LLM include-vs-exclude disagreements and exclude maybe-vs-yes disagreements.
The existing human-vs-llm filter still returns raw Human vs LLM answer disagreements under the new Human vs LLM conflict label.
Route tests cover page, count, and export behavior for differenceFilter=human-vs-llm-true-conflict.

userStories.title: Expose comparison stats API and client service
userStories.description: As a client developer, I want a comparison stats endpoint and typed service wrapper so the page can load stats separately from paginated judgment rows.
acceptanceCriteria: Add GET /api/comparison-projects/:id/stats and return activeGeneration, isServingReady, servingStatus, servingUpdatedAt, and comparisons.
The stats route returns empty comparisons when there is no active serving generation or no comparable columns.
The stats route reads the active comparison serving generation rather than scanning raw judgments on page load.
src/services/comparisonProjectsService.ts defines ComparisonProjectStats types and fetchComparisonProjectStats.
Route tests verify response shape, serving metadata, empty states, conflict counts, true-conflict counts, and kappa values.

userStories.title: Render Project Stats card on Compare Project Judgments
userStories.description: As a reviewer, I want a Project Stats card on Compare Project Judgments so I can see conflict counts, true-conflict counts, and summary-mode kappa before reviewing rows.
acceptanceCriteria: CompareProjectJudgmentsPage queries fetchComparisonProjectStats with a separate TanStack Query key.
The Project Stats card appears after the existing project details container and before serving-status banners.
The card shows comparison label, overlap, conflicts, true conflicts, and Cohen's kappa.
Cohen's kappa is formatted to three decimals when present and N/A when null.
The card includes user-facing true-conflict info copy explaining that Maybe counts as Yes/include and true conflicts are Include vs Exclude.
The card has inline loading and empty states and does not add a full-page spinner.
The existing difference filter dropdown shows Human vs LLM conflict and Human vs LLM true conflict when available.
The shared web/browser Compare Project Judgments flow is checked for the stats card and filter labels; desktop impact is considered because this is shared UI.
